A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMETH and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original unconditional and conditional graph-generation experiments in Section 4 and Tables 1–5, with experimental details and generated samples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline reevaluations and sampling-budget experiments in Appendix D, Tables 7–9.

M1.justification: Both versions use marginal node/edge CTMC rates, cosine scheduling, cross-entropy training, the graph transformer with RRWP encodings, tau-leaping with optional predictor-corrector sampling, and classifier-free guidance. The rewritten exposition and new sensitivity experiments do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate PLANAR, SBM, QM9, MOSES, and GuacaMol, including QM9 generation conditioned on dipole moment and HOMO energy. The added sampling-budget experiments retain existing datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged. DIGRESS and GRUM already participated in the synthetic comparisons; v2 reevaluates them without introducing different comparison methods. Newly cited autoregressive methods are not added to the reported benchmarks.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a controlled sweep over seven sampling budgets from 10 to 1,000 evaluations on PLANAR, SBM, QM9, and MOSES. Existing splits, metrics, and stated main-experiment settings are retained. However, v2's SBM main results match Table 7's 500-step row while Appendix C.1 still specifies 1,000 steps, leaving their actual setting unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing predictor-corrector comparisons, v2 adds a systematic sampling-budget sensitivity study across four datasets in Tables 7–9. This directly tests the central quality-efficiency tradeoff and performance saturation. Section 3 also newly reports qualitative findings favoring cross-entropy over ELBO optimization and cosine over constant scheduling.

E5.justification: v1 reports five-run means and 95% confidence intervals for COMETH but supplies synthetic baseline scores without uncertainty. v2 explicitly reevaluates DIGRESS and GRUM over five runs and adds confidence intervals. COMETH's existing reporting practice and run counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises numerous synthetic results. For SBM, GRUM's VUN changes from 85 to 69.0±8.5 and COMETH's from 75±3.7 to 77.0±5.3, reversing their ordering by reported mean. Tables 7–9 add extensive sampling-budget results; molecular and conditional Tables 2–5 remain unchanged. The SBM setting inconsistency prevents treating its revised scores as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 replace the discrete-time review with additional CTMC evolution and ELBO equations and expand the marginal-prior derivation. The core noise-schedule, RRWP, and symmetry guarantees remain; Theorem 2 summarizes earlier Propositions 2–4. The newly added backward CTMC equation has a sign error.

C1.justification: The central novelty, graph-specific noise, RRWP expressivity, sampling flexibility, and benchmark-performance claims retain their scope. The expanded abstract foregrounds the encoding contribution and PLANAR/GuacaMol results already stated in v1's introduction and experimental discussion.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly suggests that the LSTM's GuacaMol FCD advantage may reflect COMETH's filtered training subset; v1 simply interpreted it as better distribution modeling. Appendix D adds an interpretation of sampling-performance saturation. The quadratic-complexity and categorical-only limitations are retained and relocated.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly announces an intended public code release, without supplying an access link or establishing current availability. The pseudocode, hardware disclosures, preprocessing instructions, and noise/guidance hyperparameters in Appendices B–C are otherwise essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Capasso and Bakstein, Lou et al., Zhao et al., and Jang et al.'s distinct scalable-representation work. Hoogeboom et al. disappears with the discrete-time review. These are limited updates; the main positioning relative to continuous-time diffusion and DIGRESS remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, method exposition, and Appendix A.1 undergo substantial rewriting. Sampling is discussed earlier, prior-distribution explanations expand, and the main-text RRWP propositions are consolidated into an informal theorem with formal statements retained in Appendix A.3. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds three ablation tables, redraws the transformer diagram, adjusts and relocates Figure 1, and reformats tables with expanded labels and emphasis. The document template, headings, running headers, and figure placement also change extensively. The noise-schedule plot and generated-sample images themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The new sampling-budget study supplies direct evidence for the claimed quality-efficiency tradeoff, and reproduced baseline confidence intervals make the synthetic comparisons more informative. Reorganized explanations also improve accessibility. These gains are limited by new consistency problems: the SBM main results match the 500-step ablation despite the stated 1,000-step protocol, and the added backward CTMC equation has a sign error.
